My name is Gabriela Dezotti (she/her) and I am currently a PhD candidate in the Ecology, Evolution and Biodiversity Programme at Universidade Estadual Paulista (UNESP) in Rio Claro, Brazil.
I am a member of the BioMe Group being supervised by Professor Tadeu Siqueira.
I consider myself a work-in-progress vegetation ecologist with a strong interest in disturbances. Right now, I am exploring how novel disturbance regimes affect communities in an integrated framework considering different time, space and organizational scales. My work is usually focused on fire-modulated systems, but I am also interested in other types of disturbances, such as droughts and floods. Besides my research, I am deeply interested in FAIR data management and open science practices.
You can find more about my research here. If you want to get in touch, please feel free to contact me anytime.

You can call me a half-vegetation and half-(meta)community ecologist. I am a latina from Brazil, so if you like we can talk in Portuguese! I consider myself fluent in English (but I am always trying to improve) and a beginnerish in French (we can give it a try!).
I got my BSc in Biology (2021) and MSc in EcoEvoBio (2024) from Universidade Estadual Paulista (UNESP), in Rio Claro, Brazil. Where I also worked as research technian for a year (2025) with data
My interest in vegetation ecology grew through my work with the herbaceous-shrub layer of Cerrado vegetation and through questions related to how disturbance shapes ecological dynamics. Over time, I became especially interested in understanding how fire and other disturbance regimes influence populations, communities, and metacommunities.
In my current research, I investigate how novel disturbance regimes affect ecological stability in an integrated framework that considers different temporal, spatial, and organizational scales. Although my work is often focused on fire-modulated systems, I am also interested in other types of disturbances, such as droughts and floods, and in how these processes shape tropical open ecosystems.
More broadly, I am interested in connecting community ecology, metacommunity theory, and biodiversity dynamics to better understand vegetation responses to environmental change. I am also deeply interested in FAIR data management, open science practices, and clear scientific communication.
If you are interested in discussing or collaborating on any of these topics, feel free to get in touch.
